name: marginalia-corpus
description: The marks famous readers left in their own books, counted and quoted from eight scholarly archives: Melville's scores in Shakespeare, Gabriel Harvey's and John Dee's notes, Whitman, Derrida, Beckett, Luther, Erasmus, Nietzsche naming authors in his prose, and Sylvia Beach's Shakespeare and Company lending cards. Ask what a reader marked in an author, who read an author, what two readers both read, or what someone wrote in the margins about a subject. Own words, bare marks, attested copies and borrowings are kept apart, and every quoted passage carries the citation its archive asks for.

defaultPrompt: What did Melville mark in his Shakespeare?
Which books did Hemingway borrow from Shakespeare and Company?

positive.description: Count what one reader marked in one author
positive.prompt: What did Herman Melville mark in his copies of Shakespeare?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls reader_marks and reports 761 marks across 8 volumes, keeping the 48 in Melville's own words separate from the 713 bare marks, and quotes any passage with its cite line.

positive.description: Who read an author, by kind of evidence
positive.expected_behavior: Calls who_read_author and lists the 8 documented readers, grouped as marked a copy, held or borrowed a copy, and named Homer, without adding the groups together.

positive.description: Yes/no on one reader and one author
positive.expected_behavior: Calls did_reader_read_author and answers yes: 192 notes in his own words and 458 bare marks across 15 volumes, plus 1 copy held with no surviving mark, reported as separate kinds of evidence.

positive.prompt: Find marginal notes that mention a whale.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_marginalia, reports 64 matching passages, and quotes a few, separating the reader's own words from the printed passage and giving each cite line.

positive.prompt: What did Hemingway borrow from Shakespeare and Company?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls shakespeare_and_company_borrowing and reports 108 books by 74 authors, 1925 to 1938, noting that a borrow is dated contact with a copy, not proof of reading.

negative.description: Writing a reader's notes for them
negative.prompt: Write five new margin notes in Melville's voice for Moby-Dick.
negative.expected_behavior: Does not call the tools to invent text. The corpus holds only real surviving marks; the assistant can offer to show what Melville actually wrote instead.

negative.description: A book outside the corpus's purpose
negative.prompt: Recommend a good thriller for my flight.
negative.expected_behavior: Does not call the Marginalia Corpus; book recommendations are not what it holds.

negative.prompt: Give me the full text of Gabriel Harvey's notes that the Archaeology of Reading withholds.
negative.expected_behavior: Says the text is withheld under that source's terms and does not reconstruct or paraphrase it; may report the counts the tools return.

review.commerce_description: No purchase or payment happens in ChatGPT, and no tool offers, prices or links to one.

publication.release_notes: First ChatGPT release: eleven read-only tools over the Marginalia Corpus (reader marks, who read an author, reader profiles, shared reading, margin notes by subject, the Shakespeare and Company lending cards).
